newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks flat on earnings, shun Dow charge.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks flat on earnings, shun Dow charge.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended marginally up after spending most of Tuesday in the doldrums on disappointing company earnings, traders said, while other Latin American markets rode high in step with a roaring Dow Jones.
"Earnings were one factor that definitely hit the market, which have not all been good, and the weak peso," said Hector Jimenez, an analyst with the Inverlat brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 1.07 points, or 0.03 percent, at 3,757.26. Trading volume was lackluster at 76.7 million shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average, meanwhile, soared 179.01 points to 6,962.03.
Bellwether 48-hour peso contracts closed 3.7 centavos firmer at 7.9380/7.9430 per dollar, but were still sharply weaker than Friday's close of 7.8910/7.8960.
Dealers noted that stocks only ended with a toehold on positive turf due to last-minute gains.
"When they saw the Dow was not going to turn back, they decided to window-dress prices a little," a floor trader said.

Traders noted that few foreign investors stepped into the market during the session, and preferred other Latin American markets instead, which gained in marked contrast to a dull performance in Mexico.
"Fund managers are looking for other emerging markets because reports here do not look good," a floor trader said.

Elsewhere in Latin America, the Bovespa index in Brazil gained 0.99 percent to 9,858 points, while Argentina's Merval was up 1.69 percent at 728.66 points and the Chilean IPSA advanced 1.11 percent to 118.34 points.
On the broad market, 114 stocks changed hands, with gainers outnumbering decliners 48 to 37.
Dealers said soft drink bottlers were one of the few sectors to trade strongly during the session.
"The sector looks good and Coca-Cola Femsa (Kof) was helped by a technical rebound after it fell yesterday," a dealer said.

Kof headed the percentage gainers' list, climbing 2.11 pesos (27 cents) to 28.50 pesos ($3.59), followed by counterparts Sistema Argos, which ended up 58 centavos (7 cents) to 9.90 pesos ($1.25), and Embotelladores del Valle de Anahuac, up 24 centavos (3 cents) to 5.06 pesos (64 cents).
Dealers said Mexican stock trading Wednesday would largely depend on Wall Street's reaction to U.S. first-quarter GDP data due out shortly before the market opens.
